name: Yatra Online Ltd
title: Yatra Online Ltd - 543992 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Yatra's Q4 FY26 was hit by West Asia conflict: EBITDA fell 46% YoY to INR 126m as MICE bookings were cancelled or deferred, though FY26 adjusted EBITDA grew 37.5% to INR 917m and management says Q1 run-rate is about 20% above Q4.

summary.headline: Yatra FY26 revenue less service cost rose 24.5% to INR 4,824 mn and adjusted EBITDA 37.5% to INR 917 mn, but Q4 EBITDA fell 46% on MICE disruption.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 as its most profitable year in company history, with revenue from operations up 27% to INR 10,065 mn and PAT up 28% to INR 468 mn. Q4 was weak: revenue from operations fell 14% YoY to INR 1,890 mn and EBITDA fell 46% to INR 126 mn, driven by West Asia conflict cancellations and deferrals of MICE and international group bookings into FY27. Management said Q1 FY27 run rates are about 20% above Q4 and expects H2 FY27 to be materially stronger, while reiterating a medium-term 20% RLSC and 30% adjusted EBITDA CAGR.

financial_highlights.metric: Revenue less service cost / gross margin (FY26)
financial_highlights.change: +24.5% YoY, ahead of revised guidance of 22%
+37.5% YoY, in line with revised guidance

segments.name: Air
segments.commentary: FY26 gross bookings (TTV) INR 61,874 mn, up 12% YoY; gross margin INR 2,449 mn, up 30%, with margin rising from 3.42% to 3.96%. Passenger volume was 5,395,000, up 2% for the year; Q4 air passenger volumes grew 9.6% YoY, about 2x industry.

segments.name: Hotels and packages
segments.commentary: FY26 gross bookings INR 16,578 mn, up 27%; room nights 1,936,000, up 16%; gross booking margin INR 1,534 mn, up 37%, with margin rising from 8.60% to 9.25%. Standalone hotel margin rose from 7.7% to nearly 9%, and standalone hotels grew about 32% YoY.

segments.name: Corporate / B2E and MICE
segments.commentary: 163 new corporate customers added in FY26 with annual billable value INR 9,568 mn (vs 148 and INR 7,475 mn in FY25). Q4 added 55 clients worth INR 2,709 mn, against 40 worth INR 2,234 mn in Q3. Q4 MICE and international group bookings were cancelled or deferred; retention is about 97%.

segments.name: B2C
segments.commentary: Management said B2C is about early 30s% of gross bookings and mid-to-high single-digit operating margin, and is profitable on every transaction.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term CAGR of 20% in revenue less service cost and 30% in adjusted EBITDA reiterated; management said this is not a hard guidance and applies over a 2-3 year horizon.
Q1 FY27 expected to be muted, as about two months of the quarter have already played out; H2 FY27 expected to be materially stronger than H1 on revenge travel and pent-up demand.
Hotel discount-to-gross-margin ratio expected to return to about 75% or lower in H2 FY27 from about 85% in FY26.
ROCE was about 6% in FY26 (about 4% in FY25); management said it would have been 7-7.5% without disruption and targets high-teens ROCE in 3-4 years.
Corporate credit card product expected to be ready to go to market within a quarter or two; hotel virtual card platform already live.
capex_capacity: Migration to Google Cloud and enhanced API infrastructure cited as improving hotel content distribution to domestic and international partners.
Management is investing in MCP protocol integration and agentic-ready platform; announcements expected in FY27, with some innovations 'in a matter of a couple of weeks'.
Expense management product (AI-anchored, launched recently) added 8 logos in Q3 and 8 more in Q4, with 4 live.
Dedicated mid-market corporate sales team set up in Q3 FY26; early contribution seen in Q4.
Corporate wins take 3-6 months to go live and ramp up.
demand_pricing: Q4 gross bookings up 8.3% YoY; total transactions up 16.5-16.6%; hotel room nights up 36%, hotel gross bookings up 9%.
Management attributed the Q4 MICE shortfall to Dubai and Abu Dhabi disruption, higher air fares on Europe MICE, and a 1:3 to 1:3.5 domestic-to-international MICE ticket value ratio.
Hotel average realisation per room night fell on mix shift to affiliate and domestic business away from MICE; management called this short-term.

Air net discount as a share of gross take rose to about 48% in Q4 from about 35% in Q1 FY26 (which management attributed to the Operation Sindoor period); management expects it to near 45% over the next year.
Air gross take rose from 7% in FY24 to 7.1% in FY26 (management's figures); overall gross take about 8.1%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of MICE is international versus domestic, and why was Q4 hit harder than Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said international MICE tickets are about 3-3.5x domestic value, and the disruption hit Dubai/Abu Dhabi bookings in March, a peak period. Higher airfares also raised costs on Europe MICE. Q1 FY27 run rate is about 20% above Q4, with growth in Southeast Asia and domestic.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to IT services in B2E and AI risk?
qa_highlights.answer: IT services were about 10-11% of B2E business, and about 7% of total B2E including Globe and MICE. The share was about 20% at IPO in FY24.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the air discount rising and what is the take-rate outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said enterprise customers spend about 50% more per ticket than B2C, so airlines pay better realisation on enterprise. Net take rate is improving. Discount-to-gross-take was about 61% in FY23-24 and about 47-48% in FY25-26.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 FY27 tracking better than Q1 FY26, and is the 20% growth guidance still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 20-30 model is a 2-3 year CAGR view, not hard guidance. Q1 will be muted, with recovery expected in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Hotel realisation and discount trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Discount as share of gross margin was about 75% last year and about 85% in FY26, driven by Q4. Management expects a return to about 75% or lower in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: MICE competition from listed or DRHP-filed MICE companies?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said organised MICE is about 10% of a roughly INR 35,000 crore market, and that Yatra is about the second-largest organised player. It cited exception handling and DMC partnerships as moats. MICE is 10-15% of installed base revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why run B2C at all, and will B2C be split out?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said B2C is self-funding, contribution- and EBITDA-positive, and helps with supplier deals and corporate cross-sell. It declined to segment B2B and B2C formally, but may disclose gross bookings more consistently.

qa_highlights.question: Corporate credit card initiative and its effect on take rate and ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: Product expected within a quarter or two. Airline partnerships are needed to offset card fees, or the net take rate and numerator would suffer. Hotel virtual card is already live.

qa_highlights.question: Holding company (THCL) restructuring status?
qa_highlights.answer: The Cayman and Cyprus layer collapse is still in progress across India, Cyprus, Singapore and Cayman. THCL sold about 1.8% in Feb 26 to fund legal costs, and management does not expect further sales.

risks_watch: MICE and international group bookings: Q4 cancellations and deferrals; whether deferred business returns in H2 FY27 as management expects.
Hotel realisation and discount-to-gross-margin: Q4 discount rose to about 85% of gross margin; management targets 75% or lower in H2.
Q1 FY27 muted as flagged by management; Middle East conflict and airfare inflation.
Receivable days and working capital; ROCE of about 6% vs high-teens target in 3-4 years.
Corporate credit card rollout: airline fee-sharing needed to protect the net take rate.
Management declined to segment B2B and B2C, and does not disclose advertising revenue separately.
Agentic AI and LLM channels may shift B2C demand; management said the B2E walled-garden model limits exposure.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long term and cautious on the near term. Management attributed Q4 weakness to conflict-driven MICE and international disruption and called it temporary, but gave no quantified Q1 or FY27 guidance beyond the medium-term 20-30 model. It was evasive on segment disclosure and on the holding company restructuring timeline.
key_quotes: Despite some very significant headwinds that impacted 3 out of the 12 months of the year, it's the most profitable year in the company's 20-year history.
It is a short-term blip which the industry will tide over,as soon as normalcy returns.
Several Q4 MICE and international travel group bookings were either cancelled or deferred into FY27.
So we expect the second-half of FY 27 to be materially stronger than the first half.

growth.why: Management reiterated a medium-term 20% revenue-less-service-cost CAGR (explicitly not hard guidance, 2-3 year horizon) and expects H2 FY27 materially stronger, backed partly by Q1 run rates ~20% above Q4 and 55 new corporate clients worth INR 2,709 mn in Q4, but no specific capacity additions were given and Q1 is guided muted.
